title: AGILE: Lightweight and Efficient Asynchronous GPU-SSD Integration
problem: Emerging workloads (recommender systems, graph analytics, data analytics) exceed GPU memory capacity, but existing GPU-centric I/O solutions use synchronous I/O that forces threads to stall during long communication delays, reducing utilization.
motivation: GPUs need efficient access to external memory (SSD/NVMe) for workloads exceeding HBM capacity. Current synchronous approaches waste compute resources while waiting for I/O completion.
method: AGILE is a library that lets GPUs request data from SSDs without pausing computation—instead of waiting for data to arrive, it fetches it in the background while computations continue. It uses a temporary high-speed memory cache on the GPU to hold frequently-used data. To coordinate between computation and data fetching without creating deadlock situations (where tasks wait forever for each other), it uses special data structures that don't require traditional locks.
key_novelty: Combining asynchronous I/O with an integrated GPU-based high-speed memory cache and deadlock-free coordination lets GPUs fetch data from SSDs without stalling computation.
contributions: 1.88x average performance improvement across workloads with diverse computation-to-communication ratios
1.75x speedup vs BaM on DLRM through efficient design and overlapping
3.12x reduction in software cache overhead on graph applications
2.85x reduction in NVMe I/O overhead on graph applications
limitations: Full-text not available; analysis based on abstract. Specific cache algorithms and deadlock prevention mechanisms not detailed.
